summary: You asked what the long tail actually is. Twenty-nine readers pulled roughly 1,875 rows out of the estate's own records — eleven parts of the owner decision queue, two validation queues, the roadmap, the handoff cards, five parts of the chair's diary, the rewrite plan and the Scribe design. Most of those rows are the same work written down many times over, so after merging duplicates and dropping what a later record shows finished, the real list is 58 items: 43 still open and 15 that are already done and can be struck. The prose rewrite is not in that 43 — it is banked on your word, and the chair's own note is that "until the rewrite is finished" has become the release condition for the free and paid tiers, so banking it is a real decision and not a shelving. Of the 43, twenty-three are yours and nobody else's, and that is the honest headline: the largest blocker in this estate is not unbuilt code, it is unanswered questions. Five of them are a single afternoon's work on the Scribe — a key, a database push, a price, one ruling and a flag — and they unlock a whole finished feature that has never once called a model. Three more are heavier and older: the legal sitting that nothing can launch without, the production deploy that is seventy-eight migrations and a month behind with one migration that deletes real users' content at push time, and an eighteen-item batch assembled for you months ago that still sits unanswered. I have put your decisions first because almost everything under them is built, priced and waiting; then the launch-critical endgame in exactly the order the records themselves fix — the money path with the webhook before any refund, the display trains, the last output-moving wave before the golden freeze, the review, your keystroke, your walk with one regeneration, the soak, the tuning signature last, then the push; then the rest by dependency and value, with the biggest single body of unbuilt work — about a hundred and two declared engine waves — sitting where its own gates put it. Two honest cautions. The first is that the hundred-and-two figure is the estate's own measurement and it is large; nothing in this chain makes it smaller, and it is the item most likely to decide how long the tail really is. The second is that a great deal of the last two months of judgment was made on a model seat you asked to be re-checked later, and that re-check only starts when you call it — roughly a hundred and thirty sections whose authorship cannot now be recovered, plus a hundred and forty-seven unruled rows in the older queue. It blocks nothing, but it grows every day the programme runs, and three cases have already been found where something reported closed rests on ground that was never validated.
validationState: Two queues exist and neither reports itself empty. The older one, the Fable validation queue opened 2026-07-31, had exactly one validation pass: thirty-three rows ruled on 2026-08-01 (twenty-six confirmed, six adjusted, no engineering reversals), after which forty-eight newer rows were added carrying a vetoable-veto column and no verdict at all; a later count puts the whole file at a hundred and fifty-one data rows of which a hundred and forty-seven carry no status marker, and everything below its 2026-08-10 exhaustion boundary — thirty-eight Opus-era rows — is still stamped owed. The newer retrovalidation queue, re-armed by your order at §685, has had one substantial sitting: forty-three rows ruled at §892 and twenty-eight more at §896.1, but that sitting closed partial — its completeness critic never ran and eight calls stay labelled evidence-thin rather than confirmed. Everything enrolled since is "enrolled, not ruled", and the historical strata — the dark window of about a hundred and eighteen unmarked sections, the §687–§723 run, and three cases where a closure rests on an unvalidated ruling — stay queued at your trigger. The chair has written the protocol, the provenance map and the priority strata; it will not start the pass, and it cannot: a chair re-reading its own reading is circular, which is precisely why three of the widest standing grants are named as yours to re-read rather than anyone's to re-derive.
